newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks fall, plagued by lack of buyers.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks fall, plagued by lack of buyers.

text.p: Croatian stocks continued sliding to close mostly lower on Friday in light trade, reflecting what traders attributed to a chronic absence of big buyers.

They said a period of stagnation might extend into next year as investors were not likely to return for some time amid fears about Croatia's political future and a general dullness elsewhere in Central Europe.
"This may last till after Christmas and New Year," said one trader who asked not to be named.
A shaky political situation, due to uncertainty over the health of President Franjo Tudjman and a wave of public protests, sent jitters particularly among foreign investors.
"They are still calling regularly but aren't buying anything," said a trader at a large bank, which has many foreign clients.
The day saw no trading until late into the session.
Sell offers continued to outstrip buy orders at more than 10 to one as some small investors tried to cut their losses before an even bigger fall.
Three of four active issues fell and one, Zagrebacka Banka, held its ground at 990 kuna with 1,695 shares sold. Another fully-listed stock, Pliva, was not traded.
The biggest loser was confectioner Kras, one of the investor pearls during the autumn bull run. Its shares fell 50 kuna to end at 400 on volume of 130.
Food-processor Podravka closed 20 kuna lower at 215 on volume of 1,391.
What little other buying there was took place in the same issues over and over with very small lots changing hands, traders said, also noting haggling over tiny price changes.
"Buyers are cautious about everything. Prices go up and down by one kuna or so, whereas much bigger increases meant nothing to them earlier," one of them told Reuters.
Volume shrank to 3,324 units and turnover rose to 2.1 from 1.6 million kuna, bringing the meagre week's total to six million.

The second tranch of public debt refinancing bonds traded on a turnover of some 720,000 kuna. Their price also took the brunt of the market decline, falling to 5.35 percent above par, down from 7.0 percent last week.
